# Figxit

> Figxit is a native macOS autocomplete popup for zsh, bash, and fish. It opens under the cursor as you type and lists the commands, subcommands, options, package.json scripts, and Makefile targets that fit, ranked by your own shell history. It is open source (MIT), free, and local only: no account, no AI chat, no telemetry.

Key facts:

- Platform: Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 13 or later. zsh, bash 5 or later, or fish 4. tmux is optional. No other shell or operating system is supported yet.
- Current version: 0.2.0.
- Install: download the disk image, drag Figxit to Applications, open it, and click Set Up for your shell in the setup window. It adds one line to the config file of that shell.
- Completion data: the open source Fig completion specs (700+ tools), plus the Makefile and package.json in the current folder.
- Ranking: reads the Atuin history database, read-only. Atuin is optional.
- Permissions: no Accessibility or Screen Recording access.
- Replaces: the autocomplete of Fig, of Amazon Q and Kiro CLI, and of Microsoft inshellisense on macOS. It does not have Fig scripts, dotfile sync, team sharing, or AI chat, and it does not run on Windows or Linux.
- Figxit is not affiliated with Fig, Amazon, or Kiro.

## Docs

- [Full page content as Markdown](https://figxit.com/llms-full.txt): what it does, keys, how it works, install steps, requirements, limits, privacy, credits
- [README](https://github.com/en3sis/figxit/blob/main/README.md): the complete reference, with the menu bar items, the `figxit` command, configuration, and development
- [Website](https://figxit.com/): the landing page with screenshots

## Install

- [Download Figxit.dmg](https://figxit.com/download/Figxit.dmg): the latest release as a disk image for Apple Silicon
- [Install steps](https://figxit.com/#install): download, drag to Applications, set up your shell, run `figxit doctor` to check
- [FAQ](https://figxit.com/#faq): what Figxit replaces (Fig, Amazon Q and Kiro CLI autocomplete, inshellisense) and what it does not
